text:
alex: Heads up — after yesterday's routing-policy toggle in canary I'm seeing intermittent slow charts on dashboard pages (heatmaps + timeseries). Spike in main-thread CPU and chart frameskips. Noticed load waterfall shows repeated fetches for /panel-data and kv-prefetch churn. cc @maria @sam :frowning:

maria: ugh. any errors in console or network waterfall? is this only canary region? :thinking:

alex: only canary so far (eu-west-1). No hard exceptions, just lots of `200` but repeated identical requests and several `stalled` fetch times. Devtools shows kv-prefetch eviction and re-hydration over and over.

sam: can you paste a stacktrace or the fetch snippet? also pinging telemetry — maybe our new quota routing causes prefetch concurrency to spike then evict.

lee: attaching short trace we pulled from browser debug session:
```
fetch /panel-data?id=heatmap&range=last_1h 200 120ms
prefetch kv://dashboard/tiles ttl=60 -> evicted
re-request /panel-data?id=heatmap&range=last_1h
```
(repeat 6x)

lee: also saw console warning: "KV_CACHE_MISS thrash: eviction-rate=0.8" — that matches the sawtooth pattern.

maria: did we change kv-cache TTL or prefetch window in the routing-policy toggle? I thought it was just routing weights.

sam: I remember a correlated change where we reduced `prefetch.maxTTL` in canary to 60s to lower memory footprint for Dedicated customers while testing routing fallback. Maybe that combined badly with higher prefetch concurrency.

alex: yep that sounds likely. Before change: `prefetch.maxTTL=900`, canary now 60. Also routing policy bumped `route.priority` for telemetry endpoints which may have increased prefetch fanout.

rohan: deploy-bot shows the canary rollout at `2025-11-12T03:12:00Z` with two config flags: `routing.policy=v2-toggle` and `prefetch.maxTTL=60`. (deploy id: canary-20251112-3)

deploy-bot: @channel canary rollout completed: canary-20251112-3 -> 5% traffic. See deploy dashboard: https://deploys.internal/redwood/canary-20251112-3

maria: okay plan: reduce prefetch concurrency and restore TTL for canary to confirm. Quick mitigation: set `prefetch.maxConcurrency=2` (was 8) and `prefetch.maxTTL=900` back. That should stop eviction churn.

sam: agree. Also add a short-term dashboard alert: "kv_cache_eviction_rate > 0.5" for canary and wire to a runbook. I'll own adding alert.

lee: I can roll a hotfix config to canary now. Will push patch to feature flag service.

alex: if hotfix works we can continue controlled rollout. If not, pause the whole canary. Rohan, can you prepare a rollback plan and record the rollback command? (assign to you)

rohan: on it. rollback command: `vfctl rollback canary-20251112-3 --confirm`. I'll post to incident channel if we need it.

maria: follow-ups: (1) add test for prefetch TTL x concurrency interaction in perf-suite, (2) add a telemetry metric that correlates `prefetch.requests_per_panel` with `kv_eviction_rate`, (3) postmortem if this hits stable rollout.

alex: thanks everyone. Lee — patch and ping when done. Sam — add alert + update runbook. Rohan — stand by for rollback if hotfix doesn't reduce eviction-rate within 15m.

lee: pushed config hotfix to canary: `prefetch.maxConcurrency=2` and `prefetch.maxTTL=900`. Will monitor.

sam: alert created and wired to pager. runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/prefetch-eviction

alex: monitoring shows eviction-rate dropping after ~40s. charts are smoother in EU canary. keeping an eye for 10m.

rohan: great. if stable at 15m we can proceed with slow ramp. otherwise rollback ready.

alex: closing here once we confirm 30m stability. will update postmortem draft if we need one. :thumbsup:
